intro.title: Render Props (MouseTracker)
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a MouseTracker component that captures the mouse's position on the screen and displays it. You will learn the 'render props' pattern, a technique in Angular for sharing dynamic data between components by passing a template as an input. The main technologies involved are Angular components, template references, and TypeScript for type safety. By the end, you'll understand how to make reusable components that delegate their rendering logic to parent components.
intro.usecase: The render props pattern is commonly used in Angular applications where UI components need to share behavior while maintaining flexibility in rendering. For example, in interactive dashboards, you might have multiple chart components that all need mouse tracking functionality to display tooltips or highlight data points on hover. Instead of duplicating mouse event logic in each chart component, you can create a MouseTracker component with render props that handles the tracking logic, then pass different rendering functions for line charts, bar charts, and pie charts. This pattern is also useful in form builders where different input types (text fields, dropdowns, date pickers) need shared validation or focus management logic but different visual representations.

objectives: Construct a MouseTracker component that captures mouse coordinates using Angular lifecycle hooks
Initialize and manage mouse position state with reactive properties in TypeScript
Implement a render prop pattern by passing a template reference to child components
Configure template bindings to display dynamic mouse coordinates in the UI
Apply the render prop technique to reuse mouse tracking logic across different UI presentations
Manipulate component templates to conditionally render content based on mouse position
Integrate mouse event listeners with Angular's change detection for real-time updates

steps.title: Import Component and CommonModule from Angular core
steps.instruction: Import Component and CommonModule from '@angular/core' to create the main component and enable template directives.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import both symbols from the Angular core package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing Angular core symbols
import { Component, NgModule } from '@angular/core';
steps.seedCode:
// Import Component and CommonModule from '@angular/core' here

// Your component will go below
steps.expectedOutcome: The Angular core symbols Component and CommonModule are imported, setting up the foundation for creating a component.
successCriteria: Component and CommonModule are imported from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both Component and CommonModule from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your import statement. You need to import both Component and CommonModule from '@angular/core'.

steps.title: Create the main MouseTracker component
steps.instruction: Create the MouseTracker component with the @Component decorator. Set its selector to 'app-mouse-tracker' and standalone to true.
steps.hint: Use the Component import from the previous step. The component class should be exported and named MouseTracker.
steps.expectedOutcome: The MouseTracker component is defined with proper Angular metadata.
successCriteria: The component is defined with @Component decorator, selector 'app-mouse-tracker', and standalone: true
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you have all three required elements: @Component decorator, selector 'app-mouse-tracker', and standalone: true.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component definition is incomplete. Check that you have the @Component decorator with selector 'app-mouse-tracker' and standalone: true.

steps.title: Initialize mouse position state
steps.instruction: Inside the MouseTracker component class, add two number properties named mouseX and mouseY, both initialized to 0.
steps.hint: In Angular components, you can declare properties directly in the class body. Use TypeScript type annotations to specify they are numbers.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component class will have two numeric properties to track mouse coordinates.
successCriteria: The MouseTracker class contains mouseX: number = 0 and mouseY: number = 0 properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure both mouseX and mouseY are declared as number properties and initialized to 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class doesn't have the required mouse position properties. Add mouseX: number = 0 and mouseY: number = 0 inside the MouseTracker class.

steps.title: Create the mouse movement handler
steps.instruction: Define a method named handleMouseMove in your MouseTracker component that takes a MouseEvent parameter and updates the mouseX and mouseY properties with the event's clientX and clientY coordinates.
steps.hint: The method should have one parameter (event: MouseEvent) and set this.mouseX = event.clientX and this.mouseY = event.clientY.
steps.expectedOutcome: The MouseTracker component now has a handleMouseMove method that will update the mouse position when called with a mouse event.
successCriteria: The handleMouseMove method is defined with a MouseEvent parameter and updates both mouseX and mouseY properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your handleMouseMove method updates both mouseX and mouseY properties using the event's clientX and clientY values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleMouseMove method should update mouseX and mouseY properties. Check that you're using the MouseEvent parameter correctly.

steps.title: Add basic template structure
steps.instruction: Add a template to your component with a div container that listens for mousemove events and calls handleMouseMove.
steps.hint: Use Angular's template syntax with (mousemove) event binding to call your handler function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a template with a div element that responds to mouse movement events.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your div has (mousemove)="handleMouseMove($event)" to properly bind the event.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template is missing or incomplete. Add a div with (mousemove) event binding that calls handleMouseMove.

steps.title: Display current mouse coordinates
steps.instruction: Inside your component's template, add two paragraph elements that display the current mouseX and mouseY values using interpolation syntax.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to bind component properties to the template. For example: {{ mouseX }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will show two paragraphs displaying the mouse coordinates, though they won't update yet since the properties aren't initialized.
successCriteria: Paragraphs use interpolation to display mouseX and mouseY
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both paragraphs and they use the interpolation syntax with the correct property names.
steps.feedbackWrong: add two paragraph elements in the template that display mouseX and mouseY using interpolation syntax like {{ mouseX }}.

steps.title: Create a render prop child component
steps.instruction: Create a new component named MouseDisplay that accepts a render prop function as an input property.
steps.hint: Define a new component class with an @Component decorator and an input property for the render function.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new MouseDisplay component is defined with an input property for a render function.
successCriteria: Component has an @Input() property for a render function
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but make sure it has an @Input() property for the render function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The MouseDisplay component is missing or incomplete. Create a component with an @Input() property for a render function.

steps.title: Define the render prop interface
steps.instruction: Create an interface named MouseDisplayProps that defines a render function property. The render function should accept mouseX and mouseY parameters (both numbers) and return a TemplateRef.
steps.hint: Use the TypeScript interface keyword to define the props interface. The render property should be a function type that takes two number parameters and returns TemplateRef.
steps.expectedOutcome: The MouseDisplayProps interface is created with a render function property that correctly types the mouse coordinates.
successCriteria: Function accepts mouseX and mouseY parameters
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your interface has all the required properties: a render function that takes mouseX and mouseY (both numbers) and returns TemplateRef.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition is missing or incorrect. Remember to use the interface keyword and define a render function property with the correct parameter types and return type.

steps.title: Implement the render prop template
steps.instruction: In the MouseDisplay component's template, call the render function with mouse coordinates and display the result.
steps.hint: Use Angular's template syntax to call the render function with mouseX and mouseY as arguments.
steps.expectedOutcome: The MouseDisplay component template will call the render function with mouse coordinates and display the returned string.
successCriteria: MouseDisplay template contains a call to the render function with mouseX and mouseY arguments.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling the render function with both mouseX and mouseY arguments in the template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template should call the render function with mouse coordinates. Check the MouseDisplayProps interface for the function signature.

steps.title: Use the render prop component in MouseTracker
steps.instruction: In the MouseTracker template, add the MouseDisplay component and pass a render function that returns a creative string displaying the mouse coordinates.
steps.hint: Add <app-mouse-display> to the template and bind its render input to a function that takes mouseX and mouseY and returns a formatted string.
steps.expectedOutcome: The MouseTracker template will include the MouseDisplay component with a render function that creatively formats the mouse coordinates.
successCriteria: MouseDisplay component is added to the MouseTracker template with a render function that returns a string containing mouseX and mouseY values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added MouseDisplay to the template, but make sure to pass a render function that returns a string with the coordinates.
steps.feedbackWrong: The MouseDisplay component is not properly integrated with a render function. Check the template syntax and function binding.

steps.title: Test the render prop implementation
steps.instruction: Add a mouse event listener to the MouseTracker component's template to track mouse movements.
steps.hint: Use Angular's event binding syntax (event)='handler($event)' on a container element in your template.

steps.expectedOutcome: The MouseTracker component will respond to mouse movements, updating the coordinates that can be displayed.
successCriteria: MouseTracker template contains a (mousemove) event binding that calls handleMouseMove.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the (mousemove) event binding to an element in the MouseTracker template.
